h1: Privileged User Cybersecurity Responsibilities Training Quiz & Practice Questions
subhead: Take a free practice quiz or get instant, explained answers to Privileged User Cybersecurity Responsibilities questions — least privilege, PKI credentials, and reporting requirements, without the guesswork.
metaTitle: Privileged User Cybersecurity Responsibilities Quiz & Practice Questions | Cambo
metaDescription: Free Privileged User Cybersecurity Responsibilities quiz and practice questions with instant, explained answers. Least privilege, PKI credentials, restricted actions, and reporting requirements.
whyItWorks: Privileged-user questions test the extra restrictions and reporting duties that come with admin-level access — obligations that go beyond the standard cyber awareness course — and it's easy to assume the general-user rules still apply. Cambo reads the exact scenario on your screen and explains which privileged-user-specific rule governs it.

sampleQuestions.q: Who is considered a "privileged user" under DoD cybersecurity policy?
options: Anyone with a Common Access Card
Someone granted access to a DoD information system above that of an authorized general user — for example, root, administrator, or super-user access
Any employee who has completed the standard annual Cyber Awareness Challenge
A user who has been employed by the DoD for more than five years
sampleQuestions.a: A privileged user is someone with access elevated above a standard authorized user — root, administrator, or super-user access to a DoD information system — which comes with additional responsibilities beyond the standard Cyber Awareness Challenge.

sampleQuestions.q: As a privileged user, you notice your account has access to files and systems far beyond what your actual job requires. What should you do?
options: Use the extra access if it ever becomes convenient, since it was already granted
Say nothing, since having more access than needed isn't a security concern
Report it and request that your access be adjusted to reflect the principle of least privilege
Share the extra access with a coworker who might need it
sampleQuestions.a: Report it and request your access be scoped down — privileged users are specifically responsible for helping enforce least privilege, not for using excess access just because it happens to be available.

sampleQuestions.q: What does the principle of least privilege mean?
options: Granting the minimum access necessary for a user to perform their assigned duties, and nothing more
Granting every user administrator-level access by default for convenience
Restricting cybersecurity training to only the most senior personnel
Automatically revoking all access after 90 days regardless of role
sampleQuestions.a: Least privilege means granting only the access necessary to perform assigned duties — nothing extra "just in case," since every additional privilege is also additional risk if that account is ever compromised.

sampleQuestions.q: A fellow admin is going on leave and asks to borrow your PKI certificate credentials so they can keep systems running while they're out. What should you do?
options: Share the credentials temporarily since it's a legitimate operational need
Refuse — PKI credentials are for the individual they were issued to and must never be shared, even for a seemingly reasonable operational reason
Share only the password, but not the physical CAC
Share the credentials only if a supervisor verbally approves it
sampleQuestions.a: Refuse. PKI credentials identify a specific individual and are never shared, no matter how reasonable the operational justification sounds — sharing them breaks the accountability the credential system exists to provide.

sampleQuestions.q: You notice that another privileged user's admin account appears to have been used by someone other than that person. What are you required to do?
options: Nothing, unless you can confirm actual harm occurred
Mention it casually the next time you see that person
Report it immediately through your organization's incident reporting channel
Change your own password as a precaution and take no further action
sampleQuestions.a: Report it immediately — privileged users have a heightened reporting responsibility, and suspected unauthorized use of an admin account is exactly the kind of incident that needs to reach security or your organization's incident response channel right away.

sampleQuestions.q: A privileged user is informally asked to bypass a security control to help meet a project deadline. What's the correct response?
options: Bypass the control just this once, since the deadline is a legitimate business need
Refuse — bypassing a security control is a prohibited action regardless of the reason, and the request itself should be reported if it continues
Bypass the control but document it afterward for the record
Ask a lower-privileged coworker to do it instead
sampleQuestions.a: Refuse. Bypassing a security control is a restricted/prohibited action under privileged user responsibilities regardless of intent or urgency, and being pressured to do so should itself be reported.

faqs.q: How often is Privileged User Cybersecurity Responsibilities training required?
faqs.a: Annually, in addition to (not instead of) the standard DoD Cyber Awareness Challenge, for anyone holding privileged/administrative access.

faqs.q: Who has to complete this training?
faqs.a: Only privileged users — those with root, administrator, or super-user access to a DoD information system — not general users, who instead complete the standard Cyber Awareness Challenge.

Granting only the access necessary to perform assigned duties — nothing more — so that a compromised account carries the smallest possible risk.

faqs.q: Where is this training typically assigned?
faqs.a: It's commonly listed as DS-IA112.06 on CDSE's training catalog, or DISA-US1372 on JKO, depending on which platform your organization uses.

faqs.q: What happens if a privileged user violates these responsibilities?
faqs.a: Consequences can range from suspension or revocation of privileged access up to administrative or legal action, depending on the severity of the violation.
